messages:
Chloe Martin: dropping the updated API contract for usage insights review. main asks: endpoint shapes, pagination strategy, caching, and query cost budgets. doc: https://drive.google.com/redwood/usage-insights-api-contract-draft (latest) :eyes:

Paula Mendes: ty. specifically want to make sure we can support: top routes table, route detail model breakdown, and “what changed” deltas in a single flow w/out weird client stitching.

Logan Wright: +1. also want to lock down time window constraints and rate limiting now so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner later.

Jada Williams: skimmed. I like the general pattern (list + detail + export job). a couple things:
- please don’t use page=1 style pagination. must be cursor-based.
- specify sorting semantics (stable sort key) for “top spend” lists.

Nadia Rahman: re: endpoints, current proposal:
- GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/routes
- GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/routes/{route_id}
- GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/routes/{route_id}/models
- POST /v1/analytics/usage-insights/exports
- GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}
- GET /v1/analytics/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/download
I’m worried routes/{route_id}/models duplicates what route detail already needs. maybe we just return model breakdown inside route detail? keep surface area smaller.

Felix Schneider: from console side: route list -> click route -> need model breakdown + delta vs prior period. If route detail already returns model breakdown, we can skip the separate models endpoint.

Allison Grant: +1 fewer endpoints. also fewer SLOs to manage.

Chloe Martin: ok. what if:
- list returns lightweight rows (route, total_cost, p95_latency, error_rate, trend sparkline points?)
- detail returns model breakdown + deltas + maybe small timeseries
Concern: payload size / query cost for detail.

Mei Lin: detail can be bounded. in the data model we already have hourly aggregates, we can cap to e.g. 168 points max (7d hourly) or 90 points (30d daily), depending on the requested range.

Jada Williams: we need explicit contract:
- max time range per request (e.g., 31d)
- max buckets returned
- if caller requests bigger range, respond 400 w/ error code, don’t silently truncate

Paula Mendes: agree. and for deltas we need “compare_to=previous_period” as first-class.

Nadia Rahman: on pagination: list endpoint should return {
  data: [...],
  next_cursor: "...",
  prev_cursor: "..." (optional)
}
Cursor should encode (sort_key, route_hash) so stable pagination even when costs change mid-window.

Jada Williams: pls don’t promise prev_cursor unless we implement it. I’d rather just do next_cursor for now.

Chloe Martin: ok next_cursor only. sorting:
- sort_by=cost|latency|errors
- sort_dir=desc|asc
Default cost desc.

Allison Grant: query cost budget: we should document expected p95 and DB cost. can we enforce a query budget server-side? (timeout + row scan limit)

Logan Wright: yes. we already have query governor in analytics svc. propose:
- hard timeout 2s for list, 3s for detail
- max scanned partitions per request (based on time range)
- if budget exceeded, return 429 or 503?

Jada Williams: don’t use 429 for server budget exceeded. 429 is for rate limiting. For query too expensive: 400 with code like QUERY_TOO_EXPENSIVE or 422?

Nadia Rahman: +1 400 + clear error body so console can show “narrow your time range / add filters”.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC/tenancy: every request must require org_id + project_id scoping. Please don’t allow “org only” queries in v1 unless we’re ready for cross-project aggregation + permissions.

Chloe Martin: currently doc has project_id optional. we can make it required for v1. org-level can come later.

Paula Mendes: product-wise ok. we can always add org-level rollup later. for now we’ll scope UI to project.

Kevin Osei: export endpoints: we need audit logging fields defined. contract should ensure filters used for export are echoed back in export metadata so audit event includes them (time range, region, env, deployment_mode, route filter, model filter).

Chloe Martin: got it. export create response will include normalized_filters blob (server-normalized). also export job list? (not in scope?)

Kevin Osei: no list needed for beta. but export status endpoint should include created_by + created_at and download_count.

Amara Diallo: route identifier: do we use route string in path? dynamic routes could contain slashes. I’d prefer route_id as opaque hash and route_name as display. list returns both.

Jada Williams: strongly agree. do NOT put raw route in URL path. use route_id and require it to be URL-safe.

Nadia Rahman: for list filtering by route, we can do query param route_prefix=… OR route_id=… exact. If route_prefix, enforce length min 3 and max 64 to avoid expensive contains scans.

Mei Lin: if we want prefix search, we should back it with a normalized_route_name column + maybe trigram index later. For v1, I’d avoid prefix search and just do exact match + pagination.

Felix Schneider: console can survive without search for beta. table already has sort + filters by env/region. search can come later.

Allison Grant: caching: are we comfortable with response caching? list endpoint seems cacheable per (project, filters, time_window). but data is near-real-time-ish.

Logan Wright: propose:
- server-side cache (Redis) keyed by request params
- TTL 30s list, 60s detail
- include response header X-Data-Lag-Seconds (so UI can show “data updated ~X sec ago”)

Jada Williams: also include Cache-Control: private, max-age=30 (or just avoid HTTP caching and only do server cache). We need to be careful with shared proxies.

Chloe Martin: ok: Cache-Control: private, max-age=0. rely on server cache only.

API Contract Bot: Reminder: Please add reviewers to the contract doc and tag owners for open TODOs.

Chloe Martin: reviewers: @Jada Williams @Nadia Rahman @Allison Grant @Kaitlyn Nguyen @Kevin Osei @Mei Lin @Logan Wright @Paula Mendes
TODOs I captured:
1) remove /routes/{route_id}/models endpoint; fold into route detail
2) cursor pagination: next_cursor only; define stable ordering tie-breaker
3) make project_id required (v1) for tenancy/RBAC
4) define max time range + max buckets; return 400 on violations
5) add QUERY_TOO_EXPENSIVE error code + examples
6) export status fields: created_by/at, normalized_filters, download_count; confirm audit logging expectations
7) caching: server-side only; add X-Data-Lag-Seconds header

Paula Mendes: looks good. can you also add example requests/responses (happy + error) so docs team can lift them directly?

Chloe Martin: yep. I’ll add:
- top routes list example (7d, env=prod)
- route detail example w/ compare_to=previous_period
- 400 examples for TIME_RANGE_TOO_LARGE + QUERY_TOO_EXPENSIVE
- 403 example for cross-project attempt

Allison Grant: please include p95 target in contract doc (even if not SLO doc), something like “list p95 < 700ms under typical load” so we have a perf bar.

Logan Wright: +1. and include rate limits (per project) so we don’t melt analytics svc when someone refreshes the console.

Chloe Martin: added to TODO: rate limits section. proposing 60 rpm per project for list, 120 rpm for detail (since it’s per click), exports 5/hr per project.

Kevin Osei: exports 5/hr sounds right. also add max export size + timeouts in contract (csv rows cap etc.).

Chloe Martin: ack. will update and ping when ready for re-review today.
